registeredBy: Sam (owner); same rule as version 1, registered before any method 2 run
hypothesis: When leveraged-fund positioning in a currency future becomes crowded (top or bottom 10% of the past three years), it comes back by 3 points of open interest within 8 weeks more often than after any week, and the edge survives counting cases in the same year as one block and holds in most currencies.
knownLimits: Same rule, sample and pass mark as version 1, which passed under method 1 (85.5% vs 65.8%, p 1.3e-11 with cases counted as independent). Version 2 changes only how sure the result is allowed to look.
Crowded weeks are extreme by construction, so part of any unwind is ordinary reversion to the middle; the base rate after any week does not remove that.
An unwind is measured in positioning, not in the exchange rate: it says crowding eases, not that the currency moves.
Six USD crosses move together; resampling whole years covers cases in the same year, not the size of the common dollar factor within a year.
